target_customer: Non coding individuals and makers who want to build and share native mobile apps with AI
problem: Building a native mobile app normally needs coding, backend setup and App Store accounts. Bloom lets people vibe code cross platform apps, test them on a phone in seconds and deploys a backend.
business_model: consumer and prosumer subscription for an AI app builder (pricing not shown on the site)

founders.name: David Oort Alonso
previous_startups: Fireview (declined an acquisition offer from a YC Series A startup)
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders previously built award winning consumer mobile apps including Giftit.

founders.name: Sirian Maathuis
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as a designer who also builds things.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating working native apps from prompts with live phone preview and an auto deployed backend is standard LLM tooling plus real engineering on the runtime and preview pipeline.

defensibility.rationale: Many vibe coding tools exist and the core model access is shared, so copying the experience is easy; the mobile native preview and backend are small advantages.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A January 2026 eWeek article reports Replit launching vibe coding for mobile apps, so a larger player moved into the wedge after Bloom's batch.

market_need_then: Vibe coding was a fast growing behaviour in 2025, and the founders argue other tools produce toys rather than apps with a backend. No customer or revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses bloom.diy rather than bloom.com; company entity is Bloom Labs, Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and aspirational, 'Make your ideas Bloom'

rebrands.why: PitchBook lists Fireview and Giftit as former names; the YC page says the founders turned down an acquisition of Fireview to build Bloom. Date not stated.

branding.community_and_virality: Has Discord, X, LinkedIn and YouTube channels; no press on the brand itself found

brand_strength.rationale: Pleasant word but extremely common, with many unrelated companies called Bloom crowding search; no evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Bloom is a two person company that entered YC in Spring 2025 and is still active with no public outcome. No verified funding round, revenue or user figure was found, so its trajectory cannot be judged. The founders had earlier consumer app experience and turned down an acquisition of a prior product, while the main risk is a crowded vibe coding market that platforms like Replit entered.
notes: Funding is unverified: PitchBook (aggregator) lists about $3.93M total, a $3.4M seed and investors Y Combinator, Moonfire, Pioneer Fund, S2S Ventures and Sapienta; other aggregators give conflicting figures ($2M July 2025, $125M, $9.4M for a different company). None is recorded as a round. Batch is labelled X25 or P25 by some sources. Many unrelated companies are named Bloom. No dated competitor sources near the batch were found; the competitor search returned only 2026 material.
